extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent attorneys, patent examiners, and Patent Office staff
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules and procedural/substantive requirements governing application, examination, issuance, reissue, enforcement, extensions, design patents, caveats, markings, and fees under the Revised Statutes for U.S. patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens for compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: When the invention or discovery is of a composition of matter, the applicant, if required by the Commissioner, shall furnish specimens of ingredients and of the composition, sufficient in quantity for the purpose of experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner may require specimens; sufficient quantity needed for experiment. (Section 4890)

rubrics_metrics.name: Models when representation admits
rubrics_metrics.description: In all cases which admit of representation by model, the applicant, if required by the Commissioner, shall furnish a model of convenient size to exhibit advantageously the several parts of his invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models required only when representation by model is possible and Commissioner so requires. (Section 4891)

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath of originality and citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant shall make oath that he verily believes himself to be the original and first inventor or discoverer; that he does not know or believe the same was ever before known or used; and shall state his country of citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oath may be made before authorized US officers or specified foreign officials/notaries for applicants abroad. (Section 4892)

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's examination and issuance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: On filing and payment of fees the Commissioner shall examine the alleged new invention or discovery; if it appears the claimant is justly entitled and the invention is sufficiently useful and important, the Commissioner shall issue a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuance depends on just entitlement and being sufficiently useful and important, as determined by the Commissioner. (Section 4893)

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion/prosecution within two years (abandonment rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications shall be completed and prepared for examination within two years after filing, and failure to prosecute within two years after any action of which notice has been given shall be regarded as abandonment unless delay was unavoidable and shown to Commissioner's satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-year prosecution timeframe; burden to show unavoidable delay to avoid abandonment. (Section 4894)

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee applications and recordation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents may be granted or re-issued to the assignee, but assignment must first be entered of record in the Patent-Office; in all cases of an application by an assignee the application shall be made and the specification sworn to by the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment must be recorded prior to effectiveness against subsequent parties; inventor must make application and swear to specification even if assignee applies. (Section 4895)

rubrics_metrics.name: Executor/administrator filing on applicant's death
rubrics_metrics.description: If inventor dies before a patent is granted, the right to apply devolves on executor/administrator in trust for heirs or devisees, and the required oath/affirmation shall be varied so it can be made by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers application rights to legal representatives with modified oath form. (Section 4896)

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to pay final fee — right to reapply
rubrics_metrics.description: A person for whom a patent was ordered to issue but who fails to pay the final fee within six months after allowance may make an application for the patent like an original application, but must do so within two years after allowance; no damages are recoverable for manufacture/use prior to issue under such renewed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second application window: within two years after allowance; abandonment considered question of fact at hearing. (Section 4897)

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignability in writing and three‑month recording rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent or interest therein shall be assignable by instrument in writing; an assignment, grant, or conveyance shall be void as against any subsequent purchaser or mortgagee for valuable consideration without notice unless recorded in the Patent-Office within three months from the date thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording within three months is necessary to be effective against subsequent purchasers without notice. (Section 4898)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior purchaser's right to use pre-application
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who purchases from the inventor, or with his knowledge constructs any newly invented article prior to inventor's application, or who sells or uses one so constructed, shall have the right to use and vend the specific thing so made without liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right applies when purchase/construction occurred prior to inventor's application. (Section 4899)

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking patented articles and damages limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentees and their assigns must give sufficient notice to the public that the article is patented by fixing 'patented' and the day and year of grant or a similar label; in suits for infringement a party failing to mark shall not recover damages except on proof the defendant was duly notified of the infringement and continued after such notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marking requirement is a prerequisite to recovering damages absent actual notice to the infringer. (Section 4900)

rubrics_metrics.name: False marking penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who marks or affixes 'patent' or words importing a patent to an article for which he has not obtained a patent, or who imitates a patentee's mark without consent, or marks unpatented articles to deceive the public, shall be liable to a penalty of not less than $100, one-half to the person suing and one-half to the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty recovered in district court within jurisdiction where offense occurred. (Section 4901)

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat filing and protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any US citizen who desires further time to mature an invention may file a caveat setting forth the design and distinguishing characteristics and praying protection; caveats are filed confidentially and are operative for one year; if another application would interfere the Patent Office deposits the other application's materials in confidential archives and mails notice to the caveator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveat preserves priority for one year and triggers notice to caveator on interfering filings; aliens have caveat privilege if resident one year and sworn intent to become citizen. (Section 4902)

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat response timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: If notice is given of an interfering application, the caveator must file his description, specifications, drawings, and model within three months from the time of placing the notice in the Washington post-office, with usual mail time added and indorsed on the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-month filing window measured from mailing of notice plus transit time. (Section 4902)

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice on claim rejection and reexamination procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When any claim is rejected the Commissioner shall notify the applicant, giving briefly the reasons and such information and references as may be useful in judging renewal or alteration; if applicant persists the Commissioner shall order re-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection notices must include reasons and references; persistence by applicant triggers re-exam. (Section 4903)

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference notice and priority determination
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application would interfere with a pending application or unexpired patent, the Commissioner shall give notice to the applicants and direct the primary examiner to determine priority of invention; Commissioner may issue a patent to the adjudged prior inventor unless the adverse party appeals within a time (not less than 20 days) as prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner directs priority determination and sets minimum appeal periods. (Section 4904)

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for affidavits and depositions in Patent-Office cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may establish rules for taking affidavits and depositions required in Patent-Office cases, and such may be taken before any officer authorized to take depositions for use in U.S. or State courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner has rulemaking authority for evidentiary procedures; depositions taken per usual court-authorized officers. (Section 4905)

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoena issuance for Patent-Office testimony and 40‑mile limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The clerk of any U.S. court in a district wherein testimony is to be taken for a contested Patent-Office case shall, upon application, issue a subpoena for witnesses residing within that district; no witness shall be required to attend at a place more than forty miles from where the subpoena is served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoena power available via federal courts; forty-mile travel limit for witnesses. (Section 4906)

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness fees equivalent to U.S. courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Every witness duly subpoenaed and in attendance shall be allowed the same fees as are allowed to witnesses attending the courts of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Witness fee parity with federal court witness fees. (Section 4907)

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement of subpoenas — fees/tender and secret invention protection
rubrics_metrics.description: If a subpoenaed witness neglects or refuses to appear or to testify, the issuing judge may enforce obedience or punish disobedience; but no witness is deemed guilty of contempt unless his fees and travelling expenses and one day's attendance are paid or tendered at time of service; nor for refusing to disclose any secret invention owned by himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contempt relief conditioned on payment/tender of statutory fees and expense; secrecy of a witness's own secret invention protected. (Section 4908)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to board of examiners-in-chief after two rejections or in interferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Every applicant for a patent or reissue any of whose claims have been twice rejected, and every party to an interference, may appeal from the primary examiner's decision to the board of examiners-in-chief upon payment of the fee for such appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right to appeal after two rejections or when party to interference; fee required. (Section 4909)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Commissioner in person
rubrics_metrics.description: If dissatisfied with the examiners-in-chief decision, the party may, on payment of the prescribed fee, appeal to the Commissioner in person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further internal appeal path available to Commissioner on payment. (Section 4910)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Supreme Court of the District of Columbia
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party (except to an interference) is dissatisfied with the Commissioner's decision, he may appeal to the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia, sitting in banc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External judicial review for non-interference appealable decisions. (Section 4911)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal procedural requirement: file reasons in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: When an appeal is taken to the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia the appellant shall give notice to the Commissioner and file in the Patent-Office, within such time as the Commissioner appoints, his reasons of appeal specifically set forth in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant must file specific written reasons within Commissioner-set time. (Section 4912)

rubrics_metrics.name: Court hearing and record procedures on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Before hearing the appeal the court shall give notice to the Commissioner; the appellant shall lay before the court certified copies of all original papers and evidence; the Commissioner shall furnish the grounds of his decision in writing; at request the Commissioner and examiners may be examined under oath to explain principles of the thing patented. The court shall revise the decision in a summary way confined to the points in the reasons of appeal and shall return a certificate of proceedings and decision to be entered of record and to govern further proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court's review is summary and limited to points in reasons; full record and Commissioner's grounds required; examiners/Commissioner may be examined under oath. (Sections 4913–4914)

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy by bill in equity where patent refused
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a patent on application is refused by the Commissioner or by the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia on appeal, the applicant may have remedy by bill in equity; the court may adjudge the applicant entitled to a patent for his invention (or any part of it) and authorize the Commissioner to issue it upon filing a copy of the adjudication and complying with law; applicant pays expenses whether final decision is favorable or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable remedy available; applicant bears expenses regardless of outcome. (Section 4915)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue for defective/insufficient specification or inadvertent overclaiming
rubrics_metrics.description: When any patent is inoperative or invalid by reason of defective or insufficient specification, or because the patentee claimed more than he had the right to claim, if the error arose by inadvertence, accident, or mistake and without fraudulent or deceptive intention, the Commissioner shall, on surrender of the patent and payment of duty, cause a new patent with corrected specification to be issued to the patentee (or successors) for the unexpired term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue allowed only for inadvertent mistakes without fraud; surrender and payment required; reissue specifications subject to revision/restriction like original applications. (Section 4916)

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter in reissue except limited proof-based amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: No new matter shall be introduced into the specification in reissue, nor shall the model or drawings be amended (in machine patents) except each by the other; but where there is neither model nor drawing amendments may be made upon proof satisfactory to the Commissioner that such new matter or amendment was part of the original invention and was omitted by inadvertence, accident, or mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition on introducing new matter in reissue unless shown to have been part of original invention and omitted by mistake. (Section 4916)

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple reissued patents for distinct parts permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may, at his discretion, cause several patents to be issued for distinct and separate parts of the thing patented, upon demand of the applicant and payment of the fee for a reissue for each such patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue may produce separate patents for distinct parts; each requires fee. (Section 4916)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue has same legal effect as corrected original
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent so re-issued, together with the corrected specification, shall have the same effect and operation in law on the trial of actions arising thereafter as if the same had been originally filed in such corrected form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissued patent treated as if originally filed in corrected form for future litigation, subject to no-new-matter limitation. (Section 4916)

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer procedure for claimed parts not owned
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patentee, through inadvertence, has claimed more than he was the original inventor of, his patent shall be valid for the part truly and justly his own (if material or substantial); the patentee may, on payment of the fee, make a disclaimer of such parts not chosen to claim, in writing attested by witnesses, and recorded in the Patent-Office; the disclaimer shall thereafter be considered part of the original specification to the extent of the interest claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclaimer must be written, witnessed, recorded; affects extent of rights and is part of record; does not affect pending actions except as to unreasonable delay in filing it. (Section 4917)

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief for interfering patents by suit in equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there are interfering patents any interested person may have relief against the interfering patentee and parties by suit in equity; the court may adjudge either patent void in whole or in part or inoperative or invalid as to the parties to the suit, subject to rights of others not parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable relief to resolve interfering patents; judgments affect only parties to suit and their successors. (Section 4918)

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages for infringement and treble damages discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Damages for infringement may be recovered by action on the case in the name of the party interested; where a verdict is rendered for the plaintiff the court may enter judgment for any sum above actual damages not exceeding three times such verdict, together with costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may increase damages up to treble the verdict amount depending on circumstances. (Section 4919)

rubrics_metrics.name: Defenses in infringement actions (special matters list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendant in infringement actions may plead the general issue and, with 30 days' written notice to plaintiff or attorney, prove special matters: (1) specification made to contain less than the whole truth or more than necessary to produce desired effect (fraud/overstatement); (2) patent was surreptitiously or unjustly obtained for what another had invented who was diligently adapting/perfecting it; (3) the subject was patented or described in printed publication prior to supposed invention; (4) patentee was not original and first inventor of any material and substantial part of the thing patented; (5) it had been in public use or on sale in the U.S. for more than two years before application or had been abandoned to the public. Defendant must state names/dates of patentees, names/residences of prior inventors, and where and by whom used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These defenses, if found for defendant, bar plaintiff and may be pleaded in equity suits as well; notice and specificity requirements for prior-invention defense apply. (Section 4920)

rubrics_metrics.name: Courts' power to grant injunctions and assess increased damages
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts vested with jurisdiction under the patent laws may grant injunctions according to equity principles to prevent violation of patent rights on terms deemed reasonable; upon decree for infringement complainant entitled to recover profits and damages assessed or caused to be assessed, and court has power to increase such damages in its discretion as given in actions in the nature of trespass upon the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable injunctive relief and discretion to increase damages analogous to trespass damages enhancement. (Section 4921)

rubrics_metrics.name: Suit for infringement of bona fide part when overclaiming
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever, through inadvertence and without willful default, a patentee has claimed more than he was the original inventor of, the patentee (and executors/assigns) may maintain suit at law or in equity for infringement of any part that was bona fide his own, if it is a material and substantial part and definitely distinguishable from parts claimed without right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plaintiff may recover for bona fide part despite overclaiming, but no costs shall be recovered unless proper disclaimer entered at Patent-Office before suit commencement; benefits lost if patentee unreasonably neglected or delayed entering disclaimer. (Section 4922)

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign prior use not fatal absent printed publication and belief of originality
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall not be held void because it had been known or used in a foreign country before inventor's invention if, at the time of application, the patentee believed himself the original and first inventor and it had not been patented or described in a printed publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign prior use/patenting does not defeat patent where inventor in good faith believed himself original and no printed publication existed. (Section 4923)

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent extension application timing and required financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee desiring extension of a patent granted prior to March 2, 1861 shall apply in writing to the Commissioner setting forth reasons and furnish a written statement under oath of the ascertained value of the invention and of receipts and expenditures in sufficient detail to exhibit true account of loss and profit; application must be filed not more than six months nor less than ninety days before original term expiration; no extension after expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict timing window for extension application and sworn financial/accounting statement required. (Section 4924)

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of notice for extension and opportunity to oppose
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of extension application and payment of fees the Commissioner shall publish notice in one Washington newspaper and other papers in the most interested region for at least sixty days prior to hearing, stating time and place so any person may appear and show cause why extension should not be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notice and opportunity for adverse parties to appear required prior to hearing on extension. (Section 4925)

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal examiner report on extension—patentability at original grant
rubrics_metrics.description: On publication of extension notice the Commissioner shall refer the case to the principal examiner of the class to make a full report stating particularly whether the invention or discovery was new and patentable when the original patent was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension proceeding includes technical evaluation by principal examiner regarding original patentability. (Section 4926)

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner hearing standard for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: At designated hearing the Commissioner shall hear evidence for and against extension; if satisfied that the patentee, without neglect or fault on his part, failed to obtain reasonable remuneration for time, ingenuity, expense, and introduction into use, and that extension is just and proper with due regard to public interest, the Commissioner shall certify renewal extending patent seven years from expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension granted only on proof of lack of reasonable remuneration without patentee's neglect and balancing public interest; extension term seven years producing effective 21-year total if granted. (Section 4927)

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension benefit to assignees and grantees
rubrics_metrics.description: The benefit of an extension of a patent shall extend to the assignees and grantees of the right to use the thing patented, to the extent of their interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignees/grantees share extension benefit pro rata to their interest. (Section 4928)

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent eligibility and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who by industry, genius, and expense invent any new and original design for a manufacture, statue, bas-relief, printing designs for fabrics, impressions/ornaments/pictures to be printed or worked into manufacture, or any new useful original shape/configuration of an article of manufacture not previously known/used or described in printed publication, may obtain a patent therefor upon payment of prescribed fee and due proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patents cover ornamental designs, prints, and shapes/configurations of manufactured articles subject to novelty and non-publication. (Section 4929)

rubrics_metrics.name: Models may be dispensed for designs when drawings suffice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may dispense with models of designs when the design can be sufficiently represented by drawings or photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models optional for designs if drawings/photographs adequately represent the design. (Section 4930)

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent term election options
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents for designs may be granted for the term of three years and six months, or for seven years, or for fourteen years, as the applicant may elect in his application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applicants choose from three statutory term lengths at filing. (Section 4931)

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent extensions for pre-1861 patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentees of designs issued prior to March 2, 1861 shall be entitled to extension of their patents for seven years in the same manner and under the same restrictions as provided for extensions of patents for inventions issued prior to that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-1861 design patents have separate extension eligibility mirroring invention extension rules. (Section 4932)

rubrics_metrics.name: General applicability of patent regulations to designs
rubrics_metrics.description: All regulations and provisions which apply to obtaining or protecting patents for inventions or discoveries not inconsistent with this Title shall apply to patents for designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural and protective rules for invention patents generally apply to design patents unless inconsistent. (Section 4933)

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent fee schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated rates for patent fees: e.g., filing each original application (except designs) $15; issuing each original patent (except designs) $20; design cases: 3.5 years $10, 7 years $15, 14 years $30; filing each caveat $10; re-issue application $30; filing each disclaimer $10; application for extension $50; granting of extension $50; appeal first time to examiners-in-chief $10; appeal from examiners-in-chief to Commissioner $20; certified copies ten cents per hundred words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed statutory fee amounts for various filings, appeals, certified copies, reissues, disclaimers, caveats, extensions, and design-term elections. (Section 4934)
